subject: Determining 'threshold' (with cutoff.predictor) and missing data cutoff (for AMOVA)

messages.author: 7f8074a18bec5412
messages.subject: Determining 'threshold' (with cutoff.predictor) and missing data cutoff (for AMOVA)
parts:
Does anybody in this group have any non-poppr references for the ‘filter_stats’ and ‘cutoff_predictor’ functions? I'm just trying to figure out the methodology for calculating the distance threshold for the mlg filtering in poppr. My committee member originally suggested I use the Genodive histogram feature to determine the cutoff, but I am absolutely determined to complete my entire analysis in R and am pretty sure that ‘filter_stats’ and ‘cutoff_predictor’ do the same thing. I just need to be able to justify this and I'm having trouble finding it in the literature (maybe I'm just not familiar with the terminology for which I should be looking?).

I'm also looking for any guidelines for determining the missing data cutoff level for the AMOVA. When I look at all my papers, the cutoff either isn't reported or is reported without any mention on how they chose that level. I have a lot of missing microsatellite data and I really want to choose a justifiable cutoff level.

So if anybody has a useful reference for either of these two methodologies, or at least a direction in which I should look, please let me know!

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Determining 'threshold' (with cutoff.predictor) and missing data cutoff (for AMOVA)
parts:
Hi Leah,

Thank you for posting to the group. There are no references for cutoff_predictor() other than the 2015 Frontiers paper and its supplementary material (where we ran a bunch of simulations and tested to see if we could pull out the clones) [1, 2]. Beyond the paper, I've also attempted to write up the methodology for choosing a threshold in the manual [2]. As I mention there, the process is to find the largest distance gap between thresholds, but it's not a perfect solution since it WILL give you an answer even if one doesn't really exist (for example, if you run it on the nancycats data set, it will tell you that the cutoff is a dissimilarity distance of 0.25, which is bonkers considering that cats are not normally clonal), which is why the histogram is plotted underneath for visual inspection. Beyond that, you might also want to check out The RClone package [4], where they have outlined a method that uses simulated scenarios to determine the cutoff threshold.

Regarding missing data cutoff for AMOVA, This was written to mimic the behavior of Arlequin, which uses a default cutoff of 5% (any loci with more than this were dropped). That being said, the Euclidean distance can handle missing data (as long as you have some loci comparable between all individuals), so you should be able to run it by setting missing = "asis".

I hope that helps. Please do not hesitate to reply if you need clarification.

Best,
Zhian


[1]: https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2015.00208
[2]: https://htmlpreview.github.io/?https://github.com/grunwaldlab/supplementary-poppr-2.0/blob/master/Rscripts/mlg_filter_stats.html
[3]: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/articles/mlg.html#choosing-a-threshold
[4]: https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210x.12550

messages.author: 2d273081e5c65c66
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Determining 'threshold' (with cutoff.predictor) and missing data cutoff (for AMOVA)
parts:
Hi Leah,
I don't have more references but I can tell you how I've used that functions.
First of all, the filter_stats function applied to the genclone object, using all the algorithms (Nearest, UPGMA and Farthest), which will give you a list$thresholds with the thresholds you are looking for. As mentioned by Zhian, you'll also get a plot with histograms and coloured dots related to the algorithms. There I got a clear gap between two values, guiding me to the proper threshold. Here my first code:
fil_stat <- filter_stats(clone_kno_corr, distance = bruvo.dist, replen = psarep, plot = TRUE, stats = "all")

Then, I extracted only the thresholds related to the algorithm I wanted to use (UPGMA):
thre_ave <- fil_stat$average$THRESHOLDS
 
And applied cutoff_predictor:
cut_ave1 <- cutoff_predictor(thre_ave, fraction = 1)
Here I noticed that fraction = 1 will take the whole bunch of thresholds, which makes the calculation meaningful in my opinion (you could use 0.5  for example and take half of them but for me it doesn't make sense).
Like this I got my cutoff which was perfectly in line with the plot and also with this dataset. Seems obvious but in other cases the plot was not that clear and the analysis was a bit more tricky.

I hope it's clear and may be helpful to you! :) 
Have a nice day,

Silvia
